A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BevSplat by the same authors. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original KITTI and VIGOR localization results, backbone and rendering ablations, and initialization-error experiments in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 reports original localization results, expanded ablations, computational measurements, and multi-frame experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: V1 learns depth-bucket probabilities and pretrains Gaussian geometry using image/depth reconstruction losses. V2 instead initializes geometry from pretrained depth and learns Gaussian offsets, scales, rotations, and opacities through ResNet/MLP modules. UniK3D replaces icosphere-based panoramic supervision, and Section 4.3 adds Transformer-based multi-frame fusion.

E1.justification: KITTI and VIGOR coverage, including their geographic evaluation regimes, remains. V2 additionally evaluates KITTI video queries containing multiple frames with known relative poses; v1 mentioned temporal information only as future work.

E2.justification: DenseFlow is added to both main benchmark comparisons, while HC-Net's unknown-orientation VIGOR entries are removed. The ablations add direct point projection, fixed-parameter Gaussians, DINOv1, and plain DINOv2. V1's FiT-backed 'Dino' corresponds to v2's DINOv2(FiT), rather than being another new comparator.

E3.justification: The reported batch size changes from 12 to 8 and KITTI training from 3 to 6 epochs; VIGOR remains at 10 epochs. The controlled rendering comparison switches from a shared VGG backbone to DINOv2. New protocols vary primitive count, Gaussian parameter bounds, and video sequence length, while the principal dataset splits and localization metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands the analyses with direct-projection and fixed-versus-optimized Gaussian controls, additional backbone comparisons, primitive-count and offset/scale sensitivity studies, temporal analyses, and explicit failure cases. Initialization-error robustness is retained as Table 5, formerly Table 4; the reconstruction and icosphere-supervision visualizations are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. V2's added plots report localization-error summaries without introducing statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The revised method and training settings produce replacement results throughout the main tables. For example, KITTI Same-Area mean error without GPS loss changes from 6.63 to 5.82 m, and VIGOR aligned Same-Area mean with GPS loss from 3.28 to 2.57 m. CCVPE's aligned Same-Area VIGOR mean also changes from 3.37 to 3.60 m. V2 adds substantial ablation, temporal, and resource results; these are not controlled version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 adds explicit panoramic direction and offset-based Gaussian definitions in Section 3.1. It also replaces v1's BEV-camera construction identifying z_min with scene height with a consistent Y-axis/XZ-plane account in Appendix E. These are localized mathematical revisions; neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction drop icosphere-based panoramic supervision as an explicitly claimed contribution, removing a prominent component of v1's contribution statement. The conclusion also removes the claim of memory-efficient, on-device suitability. The central claim about feature-based Gaussian localization remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking direct-projection failures to sparsity and occlusion and attributing improvements to learned Gaussian attributes. Appendix C identifies ambiguity on feature-scarce roads, while Section 4.1 and Appendix F explain inference-memory and rendering-speed limitations. These materially expand v1's account of mechanisms and applicability.

D1.justification: V2 adds dataset-specific feature-extractor weight sharing, explicit feature dimensions, fixed-Gaussian settings, and offset/scale defaults, alongside memory and timing measurements. Core optimizer and hardware information is retained, with revised batch and epoch settings documented. Both versions promise code, data, and weights without supplying a release link.

R1.justification: The positioning relative to weakly supervised G2SWeakly remains. V2 adds discussion distinguishing its setting from GaussianBEV and GaussianLSS, cites newer localization and reconstruction work, and introduces UniK3D and CVLNet references. References supporting the removed PixelSplat and panoramic-supervision pipeline disappear.

P1.justification: The Gaussian-generation and ablation sections are substantially rewritten, with clearer subdivision of rendering alternatives and backbone comparisons. Visualization discussion is reorganized, coordinate and impact material moves into expanded appendices, and multi-frame localization receives a separate section.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, and the framework diagram is redrawn. The combined rendering/backbone table becomes separate expanded tables. Reconstruction and icosphere figures are removed, while new sensitivity plots, failure galleries, temporal visualizations, and a coordinate diagram substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for the Gaussian representation through direct-projection and fixed-Gaussian controls and broader ablations. V1 asserted on-device suitability without computational measurements; v2 quantifies memory and rendering costs and documents concrete failure conditions. Method and training revisions limit direct interpretation of changed scores, but the stronger controls and better-supported applicability boundaries establish a substantial overall quality improvement.
